memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The elders of the community are to lay their hands on the bull's head before the LORD, and the bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD. Then the anointed priest is to take some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting."'" - Lev 4:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Thousands of people have sinned, but not thousands of hands can fit on one bull's head. So the elders lay their hands on behalf of everyone.

This is representation. A few stand in for the many, and what they do counts for all.

It is a principle woven right through Scripture, and it reaches its climax in Christ. Paul draws the great comparison: just as one man's disobedience brought condemnation to all, so one man's obedience brought righteousness and life to all who are in Him (Rom 5:18-19). Adam represented us in our fall. Christ represents us in our salvation.

That is why the gospel can be received rather than achieved. You did not earn your standing before God; you receive what your Representative accomplished. Caiaphas said more than he understood when he remarked that it was better for one man to die for the people (Jn 11:50).

There is also a lesson for those who lead. The elders here take public responsibility for what the community has done. They do not distance themselves or point at the guilty. They put their hands on the head and identify with the failure.

That is what godly leadership looks like — standing with people, not above them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I understand my salvation as something Christ accomplished on my behalf, not something I contributed to?
2. Where could I take responsibility alongside others rather than distancing myself from them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You stood in my place and did what I never could. Thank You for representing me before the Father, and teach me to stand with others rather than above them. Amen.
